from collections import deque
def rects(Iin):
    h=len(Iin);w=len(Iin[0])
    R=[]
    for r1 in range(h):
        for c1 in range(w):
            if Iin[r1][c1]!=1: continue
            # expand max square-ish rect with this top-left, border all 1
            best=None
            for height in range(1,h-r1+1):
                for width in range(1,w-c1+1):
                    r2=r1+height-1; c2=c1+width-1
                    if r2>=h or c2>=w: continue
                    border=all(Iin[a][b]==1 for a in (r1,r2) for b in range(c1,c2+1)) and all(Iin[a][b]==1 for b in (c1,c2) for a in range(r1,r2+1))
                    if border:
                        R.append((r1,c1,r2,c2)); break
                else: continue
                break
    return R
def interiors(R,Iin):
    h=len(Iin);w=len(Iin[0]);res=set()
    seen=set()
    for r1,c1,r2,c2 in sorted(R,key=lambda t:(t[2]-t[0],t[3]-t[1])):
        new=[p for p in ((i,j) for i in range(r1+1,r2) for j in range(c1+1,c2)) if True]
        # keep only if strictly inside and not overlapping smaller rect interior
        res|=set(new)
    return res

def f3(I):
    h=len(I);w=len(I[0])
    R=sorted(rects_of(I),key=lambda t:(t[2]-t[0]+1)*(t[3]-t[1]+1))  # ascending area
    seeds=[(r,c,I[r][c]) for r in range(h) for c in range(w) if I[r][c] not in (0,1)]
    out=[row[:] for row in I]
    for a in range(h):
        for b in range(w):
            if I[a][b]==1:
                cands=[t for t in R if t[0]<a<t[2] and t[1]<b<t[3]]
                if not cands: continue
                t=min(cands,key=lambda t:(abs(t[0]+t[2]-2*a)+(abs(t[1]+t[3]-2*b))))
                cy=(t[0]+t[2])//2; cx=(t[1]+t[3])//2
                ds=sorted((abs(s[0]-cy)+abs(s[1]-cx),s[2]) for s in seeds)

    return out

def nearest_seed(I,O=None):

I need to figure out the rule. The key insight: painted cells are interiors of all frames, each frame colored uniformly with the seed inside it. Frames without seeds must get a color too. Looking at the output colors per frame in demos — e.g. D1 frames (20,22)-(22,24) area painted 2 but no seed inside; other 3-painted ones have seeds of 3 nearby.

Wait — this is about overlapping rectangles. Actually maybe the real structure: there are exactly N maximal non-overlapping "frame rings" (like concentric layers). Think of the whole thing as a set of nested/overlapping hollow rectangles; each maximal region... 

Alternative simpler idea from the summary: paint every maximal all-1 rectangle frame whose interior contains a seed; cells not in such interior stay 0. Check D1 residuals (20,15),(20,16),(21,15),(21,16) expected 2, my prediction 3. Those cells lie only in frame (19,14,22,17)? Its interior is rows 20-21, cols 15-16 → yes, that's the frame. Interior has seed 3? Seed 3 is at (28,17) — outside. So interior has no seed, yet gets colored 2. Hmm, so frames without seeds get some color too.

        # take majority / any seed

        cnt=Ct(cand)
        seed=cnt.most_common(1)[0][0] if cnt else None
        frs.append((r0,r1,c0,c1,len(c1-c0)*(r1-r0)*0,(r1-r0)*(c1-c0),seed))
